title: feat: add z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx via OpenRouter
author: tomdacatto
pr_body_excerpt:
- Adds `z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx` (Z.ai GLM-5.3 FlashX, text + image in, text out) via OpenRouter, paid-only, no aliases.
- Route pinned to Z.AI `z-ai/fp8` (OpenRouter's only endpoint for this model), `allow_fallbacks: false`. No fallback: none found. The sibling `glm-5.3-flash` runs on Fireworks, but FlashX there is unconfirmed.
- Cost $0.37 in / $0.075 cached / $1.25 out per 1M, x1.055 OpenRouter fee (#14895). 1M context, 131K max output.
- Video input is not exposed. OpenRouter lists it, but it is untested here.
- Reuses the existing Z.ai logo.

**Verification**
- Registry, config, availability, resolver test and price snapshot are updated. Not run locally (sandbox can't run the Vitest/Workers suites); CI is the check.
- No live probe: no OpenRouter key in this environment. Needs a live text + image request before merge.
- GLM-5.3 and 5.3-flash use a mandatory-reasoning transform. I didn't apply it here because FlashX's behavior is unverified. Check whether reasoning-off requests need it.

Related: #5321

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Fixes #15313

gist.headline: FlashX joins the hive
gist.blurb: A fast new Z.ai brain has landed in the garden. GLM-5.3 FlashX can read both words and pictures, then return a useful little burst of text.
gist.summary: Added the paid-only `z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx` model via OpenRouter, pinned to Z.AI's `z-ai/fp8` route with fallbacks disabled, supporting text and image input, text output, a 1M-token context window, and up to 131K output tokens.
gist.impact: Developers can now call GLM-5.3 FlashX for large-context text-and-image prompts through the unified text API, with deterministic Z.AI routing and no unexpected provider fallback.
gist.visual_concept: Depict FlashX as a tiny, quick messenger spark moving from a picture card and a long scroll of text into a cozy Z.ai-powered retro terminal. Polli, wearing little aviator goggles, helps feed the terminal both a pixel landscape image and an enormous scroll, while code-plants and the existing Z.ai logo motif establish that this is a new multimodal model route.
